header.description: Layer-band attention patching as ONE document. A band patches the complete attention_output at every layer in the span during the SAME forward pass, and the sweep language genuinely cannot express that - one start-layer value would have to expand into four or eight dependent writes, and a sweep expands one axis into independent points. Two mechanisms carry it. 'intervened_models' names the set of writes in force for one forward, so several bands - overlapping ones included - are several entries over ONE table of per-layer writes; that is one model load for every band, not one per band. And 'at_once' (sec. 3.1) declares that table: the three entries below with an at_once axis denote 8 sites, 8 reads and 8 writes, and each band names the interval it means rather than listing four names. Scale this by moving the at_once range, not by adding entries - a 40-layer tower is the same three entries and one more line per band. For scale, every 5- and 10-layer band of a 40-layer tower is 40 writes and 67 intervened_models (36 five-layer and 31 ten-layer bands) in one document. Note the two widths here share their writes: band8_L9 is band4_L9's and band4_L13's writes together, and each write is authored once.
